claim: Without outside signals, prompted self-correction of reasoning does not help and usually lowers accuracy (GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9->74.7, CommonSenseQA 75.8->41.8; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5->89.0).
agent_test: Equal tokens: a prompted review-and-fix pass vs no pass on our agent; report right-to-wrong and wrong-to-right rates.
audit_note: Matches Huang et al. Tables (GPT-3.5 GSM8K 75.9->74.7, CSQA 75.8->41.8, GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5->89.0, all round 2); Kamoi abstract corroborates.

claim: Reported self-correction gains in earlier papers came largely from oracle stopping (gold label), weak first prompts, or unequal compute; with oracle stop GSM8K GPT-3.5 goes 75.9->84.3 (Huang et al. 2024).
agent_test: Re-run any gain with the stop decision made by the agent, never by a label, and match sample count.
audit_note: Huang et al. report GPT-3.5 GSM8K oracle 75.9->84.3; 95.5 is GPT-4's standard-prompt score, not a GPT-3.5 oracle result.
claim_before_audit: Reported self-correction gains in earlier papers came largely from oracle stopping (gold label), weak first prompts, or unequal compute; with oracle stop GSM8K GPT-3.5 goes 75.9->95.5.

claim: Multi-agent debate is not better than self-consistency at equal number of responses (GSM8K GPT-3.5: SC 6=85.3, 9=88.2 vs debate 83.2, 83.0). Gap search: Mirzaei 2026 (d01) also finds debate below the equal-cost baseline in all its comparisons (Qwen2.5 1.5B to 7B).
agent_test: Compare a critique round vs extra sampled votes at equal tokens.

claim: Models are poor at locating their own reasoning errors (best 52.87 for GPT-4 on BIG-Bench Mistake); the bottleneck is finding the mistake, not fixing it.
agent_test: Measure the agent's step-level error-location accuracy on a labelled trace set before trusting any step-level trigger.

claim: Given the true error location, correction gives large gains (+18 to +44 on wrong traces, 0 to -11 on right traces); a random location gains less and hurts more. A trigger needs high precision to pay.
agent_test: Sweep trigger precision and recall in simulation to find the break-even point.

claim: Models do not judge their own outputs better than they generate them (54 of 56 tests do not reject the null); sound external verifiers help while own-verification hurts (graph colouring: 1/100 with GPT-4 as own verifier vs about 40% with a sound verifier).
agent_test: Replace model self-judgement by code checks wherever a checker exists.
audit_note: Jiang et al. (54 of 56 experiments' p-values above 0.05; Table 2 caption has a typo) and Stechly et al. (graph colouring: 1 of 100 with self-critique vs nearly 40% with sound verifier) match; Stechly 2024 abstract also reports self-critique collapse.

claim: Contested: intrinsic self-correction may work at temperature 0 with fair prompts (CSQA 75.92->76.00 at T=0; -1.89 at T=1.0). The result is flat, not a real gain.
agent_test: Run refine at T=0 with a neutral prompt and test for non-negative net change.

claim: Trained (not prompted) refinement can give a positive net gain: SCoRe MATH (Gemini 1.5 Flash) delta +4.4, wrong-to-right 5.8%, right-to-wrong 1.4% vs base 15.8%; HumanEval (Gemini 1.0 Pro) +12.2. On MATH the gain comes mostly from not breaking correct answers; on HumanEval it comes mostly from more wrong-to-right fixes. Xiong et al. (Qwen2.5-Math-7B) give a second group with a similar small gain (MATH500 78.6 vs 76.8 single-turn DPO, single greedy runs).
agent_test: Log the right-to-wrong rate of our revise step; target below 2%.
audit_note: All numbers match (SCoRe MATH +4.4, 5.8%/1.4%, base right-to-wrong 15.8%; HumanEval +12.2; Xiong 78.6 vs 76.8), but 'gain comes mostly from not breaking correct answers' holds only for MATH; on HumanEval the gain is mostly more wrong-to-right fixes (7.9%->15.2%), and Xiong's gain also comes from fixes (6.0 vs 0.2).
claim_before_audit: Trained (not prompted) refinement can give a positive net gain: SCoRe MATH (Gemini 1.5 Flash) delta +4.4, wrong-to-right 5.8%, right-to-wrong 1.4% vs base 15.8%; HumanEval (Gemini 1.0 Pro) +12.2. The gain comes mostly from not breaking correct answers. Gap search: Xiong et al. (d12, Qwen2.5-Math-7B and Llama-3) give a second group with a similar small gain (MATH500 78.6 vs 76.8 single-turn DPO).

claim: Offline SFT or STaR on correction traces fails to give a gain on MATH (deltas -14.2 to +1.8 vs base -11.2) because of distribution shift and collapse to minor or no edits; Kumar et al. argue self-generated on-policy data is required and add a two-stage multi-turn RL design to avoid collapse (RISE reports gains with iterative on-policy fine-tuning).
agent_test: Not testable without training; use as warning when proposing learned triggers.
audit_note: Kumar et al. Table 1 (MATH) deltas are -14.2 to +1.8 (STaR -14.2, Pair-SFT +1.8), not -11 to +2 (-11.2 is the base model); failure modes (distribution shift, collapse to minor/no edits) match, but the paper argues on-policy data fixes shift while collapse needs SCoRe's two-stage design, and RISE (iterative on-policy fine-tuning, not RL) also reports gains, so 'on-policy multi-turn RL is needed' is too strong.
claim_before_audit: SFT or STaR on correction traces fails (deltas -11 to +2) because of distribution shift and collapse to no edits; on-policy multi-turn RL is needed.

claim: ReVISE: a learned [eos]/[refine] token after the first answer beats SFT/RFT/STaR+ at Maj@1 by about 1.9 to 2.8 points (1B GSM8K 28.1 vs 26.2; 8B GSM8K 61.6 vs 59.2; 8B MATH-500 33.6 vs 30.8). Table values re-checked in the PDF. Gap search: no independent run of ReVISE itself; a related self-rewarding recipe (d12) shows the same 1 to 3 point size. ReVISE MATH-to-GSM8K transfer edge is only +0.6 (1B) and +1.2 (8B) (d13).
agent_test: Replicate on a different model family, at equal tokens against best-of-2.

claim: ReVISE's own verify signal has AUROC 76.0 vs V-STaR 69.5; the curriculum raises it from 71. An AUROC of 76 is weak for a trigger. Gap search: no-training verbalized confidence from reasoning models reaches AUROC 66 to 79 on math from one sample (d07), and a 2-sample hybrid adds up to +12.9 (d08); so 76 is not special.
agent_test: Compute the AUROC of our own trigger signal against correctness.

claim: ReVISE confidence-weighted voting beats plain majority only modestly (33.9 vs 33.2 at 8 samples; Maj@64 37.7 vs 33.2).
agent_test: Weight votes by trigger probability vs unweighted at equal samples.

claim: ReVISE matches SCoRe on Gemma-2-2B MATH-500 (23.2 vs 23.0) with about 1/30 of the generations (50k vs 1.5M); more rounds reach 25.8.
agent_test: None (training cost claim).

claim: Boundary: on an instruction-tuned base, plain fine-tuning falls below zero-shot CoT (1B-Instruct GSM8K 48.6 vs SFT 41.9) while ReVISE rises to 52.3; out-of-domain transfer is weaker; stage 2 slightly lowers verification accuracy.
agent_test: Check the trigger on out-of-domain items.

claim: Small models need a strong verifier to self-correct: a self-trained verifier adds little (LLaMA-2-13B correction contribution 10.8% self vs 15.6% GPT-4 verifier).
agent_test: Use a code or stronger-model checker for small base models.
audit_note: Zhang et al. Table 2 (GSM8K, LLaMA-2-13b-chat, SCORE refiner): self verifier contribution 10.8 vs GPT-4 verifier 15.6 match; 'self-trained verifier' is loose wording (the verifier is the model itself), and the other source (SelfCheck) does not address small models, so support is one paper.

claim: Self-repair in code, once repair cost is counted, gives about 1.05x or 0.97x the pass rate of equal-budget resampling; feedback quality is the bottleneck.
agent_test: Always compare refine against pass@k resampling at matched tokens.

claim: Test-execution feedback (Reflexion) and tool feedback (CRITIC) deliver the real gains: HumanEval 91 vs 80; TabMWP +4.7/+9.4/+16.0 by model size. The external signal is the driver.
agent_test: Make test or tool outcomes the S5 trigger where available.
audit_note: Minor: Reflexion's tests are model-written, and 80% is a prior-reported GPT-4 baseline; 'external signal is the driver' is the authors' framing but matches the Rust ablation.

claim: Learned and generative verifiers help best-of-N: a 6B generator plus verifier beats a fine-tuned 175B on GSM8K; GenRM GSM8K 73->93.4; PRM 78.2% on a MATH subset.
agent_test: Compare verifier-weighted vote vs plain vote at equal samples.

claim: A naive revision model flips about 38% of correct answers to wrong; a verifier or sequential vote is needed to realise gains.
agent_test: Never accept a revision without a selector.
audit_note: 38% is measured for one model (PaLM 2-S revision model) in Snell et al.; SCoRe shows a different figure (15.8% right-to-wrong) for a different setup.

claim: Hidden-state probes can predict the correctness of intermediate answers (ROC-AUC above 0.7, ECE below 0.1; above 0.9 for a 32B distill on AIME); transfer across domains is unstable.
agent_test: Not available for API models; use logprob proxies instead.

claim: LLMs correct an injected error in the user turn but miss the same error in their own output (64.5% blind spot over 14 models); appending Wait cuts it 89.3%, 5,306 training traces cut it 76.0%. Gap search: Self-Correction Bench reports no right-to-wrong cost for Wait (d14); d'Aliberti's forced cue shows +8.41 pp net on math but 23,500 right-to-wrong flips and no equal-token control (d05).
agent_test: Test a Wait re-check cue as a prompted re-entry at fixed tokens.

claim: Verify-then-correct RL gives large lifts on math with little SFT (S2R Qwen2.5-Math-7B 51.0->81.6), but RLVR may only narrow the pass@k boundary (base wins at large k). Gap search: on R1-style models over 90% of reflections only confirm and under 2% fix a wrong answer (d09).
agent_test: Compare pass@1 and pass@k of any trigger scheme.

claim: Spontaneous interleaved solve/verify gains are largest on small models (Llama-3.1-8B MATH500 +8.8); large models are right at turn 1 so the trigger rarely fires.
agent_test: Measure trigger fire rate against base accuracy.

claim: Moderator is task type: Self-Refine helps on preference tasks (sentiment 3.8->36.2) and not on math (64.1->64.1; ChatGPT said all fine on 94% of math items).
agent_test: Enable refine only for task types with a checkable metric.
audit_note: Three of four evidence lines are the one Self-Refine paper; the fourth (listed as 2404.17140) is a different paper (Zhang et al. small LMs need strong verifiers) that has no Self-Refine sentiment numbers. The sentiment (GPT-4) and math (GPT-3.5) figures also come from different models, so 'task type is the moderator' is one paper's cross-model comparison.

claim: Backward and per-step self-checks improve answer selection modestly (SelfCheck real-correct share 67.5->76.5 on GSM8K; Weng +1.67 avg on arithmetic).
agent_test: Use a backward check as a vote weight.

claim: Prompted self-inspection (Self-Refine, Reflexion, model-picks-best, debate) loses to plain repeated sampling at equal token cost for Qwen2.5 1.5B to 7B on GSM8K and MATH-500; all 18 self-inspection comparisons are negative. Model self-choice from 8 samples trails counting by 8.0 and 11.3 points at 1.5B but only 2.0 and 1.3 at 7B.
agent_test: Run our review pass against extra sampled votes at the same token count; report paired CIs.

claim: Spontaneous mid-trace 'Wait' shifts in RL-tuned models are rare (about 6 to 8% of traces in Qwen2.5-1.5B GRPO runs) and go with lower accuracy (2.57% vs 16.44%, N=723,200); R1 shows 0 to 0.25% on MATH-500.
agent_test: Do not count on the model to re-check unprompted; use an external gate.

claim: A forced reconsideration cue after the first answer, gated on high token entropy, improved math accuracy in a 1.5B model (0.322 to 0.406, +8.41 pp; 50,574 fixes vs 23,500 breaks) with no equal-token resample control.
agent_test: Replicate on our model, with a matched-token resample arm, and log fix and break counts.

claim: No-training confidence read-outs from reasoning models can discriminate correct from wrong answers about as well as ReVISE's learned verify signal on math: verbalized confidence at one sample gives AUROC 66.4 to 78.8; self-consistency at K=2 is lower (70.5 vs 73.5 in math); a 2-sample hybrid adds up to +12.9.
agent_test: Measure AUROC of verbalized confidence plus 2-sample agreement on our own tasks.

claim: On long-CoT reasoning models reflection after the first candidate answer is mostly confirmatory: over 90% of reflections do not change the answer, wrong-to-right is mostly under 2%, and reflection uses 16.8 to 47.8% of tokens for 1.4 to 3.5 points. Truncating it saves 24.5% of tokens for under 2.9% accuracy.
agent_test: For reasoning-model backends, skip the second pass or cap it after the first answer.

claim: In code, cheap uncertainty triggers (token entropy, verbalized confidence, entropy ensembles, semantic entropy probes) correlate weakly or negatively with pass/fail on small models, and uncertainty-triggered regeneration lowered Pass@1 in 5 of 6 configurations (-3 to -10 pp); verification-based correction gained +6 to +26 pp (HumanEval) and +8 to +20 pp (BigCodeBench) at 2.4x to 5.9x latency.
agent_test: Use a runnable checker as the S5 trigger where one exists; budget the time cost.

claim: The break-even for refine-on-trigger is a likelihood ratio, recall on wrong over false-alarm rate on right, of p*d / ((1-p)*c); with p=0.6, fix rate 0.15 and damage 1.4% to 15.8% this is 0.14 to 1.58. A trigger with recall 0.5 and false alarm 0.08 clears it and nets about +2.6 points, near reported gains. Derived, with assumed fix and damage rates.
agent_test: Measure fix rate, damage rate and trigger recall and false-alarm on our agent, then apply the formula.

claim: Training a model to verify its own solutions (RL) yields similar accuracy to generation-only training with 25% to 80% of the tokens (Qwen2.5-Instruct 1.5B/3B/7B; 7B 1152 vs 4458 tokens, 38.4 vs 38.9 average accuracy).
agent_test: Treat a verify-first habit as a token saver, only possible with training.

claim: Always-refine (label-free) prompting still overturns correct answers in recent models: Llama-3.1-8B 58.8% of correct yes/no answers overturned (accuracy -20.4); o1 and 4o overturn fewer than GPT-3.5 but not zero (o1-mini 34.0%, o1-preview 15.6% as read from a garbled table).
agent_test: Never refine unconditionally; gate on a trigger.
